verdict.rationale: The evidence shows Aider auto-committing and undoing the code edits it makes, but nothing about versioning, reviewing or rolling back automation definitions themselves. Its scripted runs (`--message`, the Python `Coder` API) and `.aider.conf.yml` config are not versioned or managed by Aider. Git history of AI code edits is an adjacent capability from a different story, and keeping scripts in git would be a user-side workaround, so neither earns credit.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can version, review, and roll back my automations
